A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The new appendix can be distinguished reliably from retained and renumbered material.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 report original finetuning performance, training-time, and GPU-memory experiments. The appendices include additional mathematical-reasoning scores and generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a Neumann-series term-count ablation on WikiText in Appendix B, Table 10.

M1.justification: The input-centric OFTv2 procedure, Cayley–Neumann approximation, custom CUDA component, and QOFT formulation remain unchanged. Disclosing the five-term configuration used in existing experiments does not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The added ablation reuses WikiText and the Llama-2 models already evaluated in Section 7.2. Existing language modeling, summarization, mathematical reasoning, instruction-following, and image-generation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same OFT, LoRA, QLoRA, and untuned-model baselines. The new appendix varies configurations of existing OFTv2/QOFT methods without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: The new ablation evaluates two through six Neumann terms for OFTv2 and QOFT on Llama-2 7B and 13B. Previously stated experimental settings remain unchanged; the five-term setting for main-paper experiments is newly disclosed rather than explicitly revised.

E4.justification: New Appendix B adds a targeted sensitivity analysis of finetuning performance versus Neumann-series term count. v1 contains no corresponding term-count ablation; the other analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new ablation follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 10 adds term-count results, including OFTv2-13B scores of 5.11 with two terms and 4.98 with five. Existing numerical results and generated examples are unchanged. The new five-term OFTv2-7B entry is 6.13, whereas retained Table 4 reports 6.14; this discrepancy is unexplained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, complexity analysis, Neumann-series expansion, and convergence condition remain unchanged. The added empirical ablation introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about scalability, approximate orthogonality, quantized finetuning, and performance. The additional evidence does not redefine their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly attributes the poorer two-term results to orthogonality approximation error and describes five terms as suitable across evaluated tasks. Existing mechanism discussions and the full-precision training-speed limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that the main-paper experiments used five Neumann terms, a reproducibility detail absent from v1. Other implementation details, hardware descriptions, hyperparameter tables, and code-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier PEFT and orthogonal-finetuning research are unchanged. The altered OpenR1 bibliography backlink reflects appendix pagination only.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical and spelling edits and inserts Appendix B. Former Appendices B/C become C/D, with corresponding contents and cross-reference updates; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 10 and introduces gray highlighting and column separators in existing tables. It also corrects the Figure 2 matrix label and a Figure 4 caption typo. Existing plots and generated-image examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B resolves an omitted implementation setting by identifying the five-term configuration and provides useful sensitivity evidence for the central approximation. Table formatting also improves readability. These are limited gains: the ablation lacks uncertainty estimates, and its five-term OFTv2-7B score conflicts slightly with retained Table 4.
